Personal Development at St Hugh's
At St Hugh of Lincoln Catholic Primary school we go beyond the expected, so that all our pupils have access to a wide, rich set of experiences. We provide these rich experiences in a coherently planned way, in our curriculum and through extra-curricular activities.
Year 1 Trip to Brooklands Museum
The children were brilliant role models throughout the day and represented our school fantastically. During the visit, we took part in two guided tours, Journey by Air and Journey by Land, where we learned about the first flight, the development of aviation and explored the aircraft factory. It was a memorable day full of learning!
Year 6 - Production of Midsummer
Year 6’s production of ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream,’ by William Shakespeare was done to an exceptionally high standard and enjoyed by all the parents who came to watch. The children brought the characters and the story to life with their skilful acting and timing. They learnt their lines impeccably well, worked as a team and thrilled us all.
Special thanks go especially to Mrs Way for her hard work and dedication in making this production so successful.
Reception - Butterfly Release
Reception have adored observing the butterflies that have emerged from their chrysalides! Although they will miss them terribly, the children decided that the butterflies would be happiest if they were released back into their natural habitat where they could continue this incredible life cycle. The children gathered in our beautiful Creation Garden to release their beloved winged friends! They shared a prayer together and even sang All Things Bright and Beautiful to celebrate the wonderful gifts of nature that God has given us!
Y5 Design Technology
It was wonderful to have the support of Lucasz from Innovate with year 5’s cooking module in DT. He taught the children so much about the essential ingredients for a bolognaise sauce and the origins of pasta.
Year 5 - Special Collective Worship Session
Our Year 5 pupils took part in a special Collective Worship session led beautifully by our Liturgy Leaders. They carefully planned and delivered the worship, sharing the Gospel reading from Matthew 19:13–15 (NKJV) – Jesus Blesses Little Children. Together, we reflected on Jesus’ love for children and the importance of welcoming others with kindness and care. The children then led the class in prayer and a time of quiet reflection, encouraging everyone to think about how we can follow Jesus’ example in our daily lives. A lovely part of our worship was sharing our class prayer book, which is taken home each week and thoughtfully added to by a different child. This week, we were proud to hear a beautiful and thoughtful prayer written by one of our Year 5 pupils. It was a meaningful reminder of the children’s growing faith and reflections. We ended our worship joyfully by singing “My Lighthouse” by Rend Collective, finishing the session with energy, smiles, and a sense of togetherness.
Wisley Gardens - Year 2
We had a wonderful trip to Wisley and the weather was glorious. The class awed at the plants in the Glasshouse, Rock Garden and a super workshop going on a nature trail and admiring all the smells in the Herb Garden.
Reception Trip to Nower Wood
What a wonderful time Reception had at Nower Wood. They were fantastic nature detectives as they used their senses and observation skills to explore woodland and pond habitats and the creatures that live there. We could not believe how teeming with life the pond was! Thank you so much to all the family volunteers who supported the children so beautifully on the day, and well done to Reception who were fantastic role models for what our school rules look like in practice; 'Ready, Respectful, Safe.'
A group of our children delivered a thoughtful and inspiring assembly all about Ramadan. They spoke confidently about their personal experiences of this special month, sharing what fasting, reflection, kindness and community mean to them.
The presenters really enjoyed answering questions from their classmates, and the rest of the school were wonderfully engaged.
We are incredibly proud of the children for leading such an informative, respectful and heartfelt assembly.
We celebrated with a Poetry Slam where every class confidently performed a poem off by heart to the whole school. We welcomed Steve Williams, author, into school on Wednesday. He kept the children entertained during his witty and educational assembly. Then he signed copies of his books for the children. I was particularly touched at how he spent time speaking with every child who came forward showing a genuine interest in them and our school. Parents have mentioned how much their children are enjoying reading his books and there are some signed copied in our library.
Our potato designing competition was linked to Steve’s books as the children were asked to make a potato look like an alien. We had some truly incredible creations brought into school.
It was lovely to see some of the amazing work produced across the school. There were examples of detailed investigations that had taken place covering all areas of the science curriculum. There were also many research projects that centered on famous scientists and their discoveries. Children across the school were given the time to visit the fair and then after school parents, relatives and friends were invited in to see some of the great work produced.
We look forward to taking some of the winning KS2 projects to the grand final at ACS school in Cobham soon, when the children will have the opportunity to look at other projects produced by other schools and visit some of the exhibits that are run by people working in the field of science.
Y5 Milestones Museum
Year 5 enjoyed a wonderful educational visit to Milestones Museum, where they took part in engaging, museum led workshops exploring the types of jobs people would have undertaken during the Victorian era and experienced a Victorian style classroom lesson with a staff member acting as a Victorian teacher, bringing history to life in an exciting and memorable way. The children demonstrated excellent conduct throughout the day and represented the school brilliantly with their enthusiasm, curiosity and respectful behaviour, which was praised by museum staff. We would also like to extend a sincere thank you to the parents and carers who volunteered to support the trip, as their time and help were invaluable in making the visit such a success.
Children’s Mental Health Week Assembly – “This Is My Place”
Our Mental Health Committee led a thoughtful and uplifting assembly in celebration of Children’s Mental Health Week. Centred around the theme “This Is My Place,” the session encouraged pupils to reflect on the spaces—both physical and emotional—where they feel safe, valued, and able to be themselves.
In their PSHE lessons, children also explored the theme by creating designs of their own “special places.” These could be real or imagined spaces, and the activity helped them think about where they feel calm, happy, and truly themselves.
Supporting CAFOD’s Refugee Appeal Through Prayer
Last term, our school took part in a Colour Run to support CAFOD’s Refugee Appeal. At the same time, some of the children who participated wrote prayers to share with their classes.
A group of Year 5 and 6 pupils then worked hard to prepare the prayers for use in every classroom. They carefully laminated, trimmed, and packed them, with a special mention to our helpful Year 6 children for their support.
The prayers are now ready to be used in classroom liturgies or at any other time throughout the year. We hope they will be a meaningful way for children to reflect and pray together. Great work year 6 helpers!
We are all part of one global family and we are called by God to care for the other members of that family, wherever they are in the world.
The children have been thinking about how they could help someone who is sad. hungry or thirsty, or poor? To help them do this and to make Jesus’ words come alive today, we invited Roy Peachey from Mary’s Meals into school to talk to the children.
Roy explained how Mary’s Meals provides life-changing school meals to children living in some of the world’s poorest communities. The promise of a good meal brings hungry children into the classroom, where they can gain an education and better opportunities for the future.
We will be organising some fundraising events for this worthy charity during Lent.
Year 4 - Trip to Haslemere Museum
They visited Haslemere Museum to explore their current History topic on Ancient Egypt. The children impressed our trip lead, Kay, with their excellent recall of classroom learning and enthusiasm for the topic. They were fascinated to learn about the mummification process, including how organs were preserved in canopic jars and the Ancient Egyptian belief that thinking was done by the heart, not the brain. The children showed great respect when viewing a real mummified body in the museum. In the afternoon, the children had lots of fun mummifying their own teddies and creating colourful masks and hieroglyphics to go with them.
KS2 Advent Reflection
What an absolute joy it was to attend our KS2 Advent Reflection this morning in church. The children did us proud and they truly captured the spirit of Advent with their speaking, singing, acting and dancing. Year 6 were word perfect in their delivery of the key lines recounting how the birth of Christ was prophesised.
We had a lovely performance by David in year 4 who played ‘Once In Royal David’s City on the organ and the choir sang ‘The Road To Bethlehem with great sensitivity.
My thanks, as always, go to our dedicated team of KS2 teachers: Mrs Way, Mr Davies, Miss Russell, Mrs Pickard and Miss Okon who led the performance and to all our support staff who worked so closely with them. Thank you to Mr Elson and to our governors for supporting the School Singing Programme and to all of you who generously donate to our School Development Fund.
The children thoroughly enjoyed finding out about how parliament works and we were surprised by our MP Will Foster who came out to see us at the end of our tour. We then headed to Tate Britain where we were surprised by some of the artworks and captivated by others. We have since written formal letters to Mr Foster to thank him for our visit and to ask him more about his role.
A group of our Year 5 children recently enjoyed an exciting Latin Experience Morning at Winston Churchill Secondary School. Joining pupils from several other primary schools, they took part in a lively carousel of activities designed to bring the ancient world to life.
The children explored Roman numerals through fun challenges, stepped into the planetarium to discover how Greek and Roman gods are linked to the stars, and worked collaboratively with new friends throughout the morning. Staff at Winston Churchill Secondary were full of praise for our pupils, whose enthusiasm, curiosity, and outstanding behaviour shone through in every session. It was a wonderful opportunity for the children to broaden their learning and experience a taste of secondary school life.
Christmas Card Design Competition - Will Forster MP
We received a phone call from Will Forster MP's office with the good news that a child from St Hugh's had won his Christmas Card Design Competition. One of our Year 2's designs was chosen out of hundreds of others from schools all over Woking. Mr Forster then joined the whole school on a 'Teams' call to announce the winner himself during our Thursday morning assembly. It was so exciting for the children. Well done to the winner and everyone who entered.
Woking Music Festival
Our KS2 Choir won the Woking Music Festival School Choirs under 11yrs category! My thanks go to Mr Ellson who has worked very hard over the Autumn term preparing the choristers so well. They sang 2 songs to a panel of judges and a large audience: Kookaburra (Sits in the Old Gum Tree) and Ain’t-a That Good News! The judges awarded them ‘honours’ which means it was an excellent performance, demonstrating fluent technical and artistic skills with emerging individuality. There was real joy to their singing and they made us all extremely proud.
Colour Run for CAFOD Refugee Appeal
To celebrate the end of term, the children, along with some enthusiastic parents, took part in a fantastic Colour Run at St Hugh of Lincoln Primary School. The playground and field were filled with laughter, bright colours and a wonderful sense of community spirit as everyone joined together for a great cause.
The event was organised to raise funds for the CAFOD Refugee Appeal, helping to support families around the world who have been forced to leave their homes. Thanks to the generosity of our school community, we are delighted to announce that we raised over £350.
A huge thank you to all the children who ran with such enthusiasm, the parents who joined in the fun (and did not mind getting covered in colour), and all the staff who helped to plan, organise and supervise the event. Your support and energy made it a day to remember.
Well done, everyone, for showing such wonderful teamwork, kindness and commitment to helping others. It was the perfect way to end the term, full of colour, smiles and community spirit.
Year 6 - Biikeabilty
Lots of the children have been out on their bikes this week learning how to cycle safely around the busy streets. The Bike Ability staff have been very impressed with their diligence and concentration.
School Celebrates Modeshift STARS Accreditation for Promoting Sustainable Travel
We are proud to announce that our school has been awarded the Modeshift STARS accreditation in recognition of our continued efforts to promote sustainable travel among our pupils and families. Wraparound Care
We run a very successful Breakfast Club and After School club (term time only) which means that we can offer wrap around quality child care where it is needed from 7.30am to 6.00 pm. Our clubs are run by fully trained school staff and is in our dedicated Wraparound Care room.
It is open from 7.30am every morning of term (apart from INSET days). Healthy and tasty breakfast options are available – a variety of cereals and hot toast. There are plenty of games to play, books to read and the space and time to finish any forgotten homework.
Open from 3.15pm to 6.00pm every day of term (apart from INSET days and the last day of term when school closes early). The After-School Club is popular and is a happy and relaxed place to finish the school day. We try to make it more like home than school and offer a wide variety of activities available to all both inside and out. It is lots of fun! We offer a variety of snacks including sandwiches, wraps and cheese and crackers. To see our three week rolling sample menu, please click this link.

Special Education Needs & Disabilities
Our Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator (SENCO) is Mrs Rachel Pickard
Email: Info@sthugh-of-lincoln.surrey.sch.uk
All children have a right to grow up in a safe, loving and happy environment. It is the intention of the school staff to take reasonable steps to ensure that the welfare of children is safeguarded and that their safety is preserved.
At St Hugh of Lincoln Catholic Primary School, we are fully committed to offering an inclusive, balanced curriculum that challenges all our pupils to achieve their best by valuing the contribution, ability and achievement of all.
We aim to promote an atmosphere and ethos that encourages spiritual, moral and cultural development to prepare our pupils to be responsible, caring members of the wider community.
Thank you so very much for all the work you have done with my son this term. I feel like it really has helped him to become so settled, calm and confident at school. He really enjoys his sessions with you, and we are so grateful for the impact you have made.
